## Goal Replace the raw-JSON presentation of a tool call in the Chat transcript with a human-readable card: a header that names the real tool behind the capability, a one-line formatted summary of the arguments actually passed, and the tool's own output (streaming while it is produced) instead of a serialized blob. The exact redacted JSON stays available in Run details. ## Current behaviour (grounded) - `desktop/src/chat/ConversationTimeline.tsx` → `TimelineCard` renders a tool card as: `.activity-icon` (icon), `{item.title}` (the capability id, e.g. `tool.shell.host`, set in `spanItem` as `string(fact.capabilityId) ?? "Tool call"`), a `.status` chip, then `ActivityData`. - `ActivityData` renders `
` with `
Input
{formatActivityData(input)}
` and the same for Output, where `formatActivityData` is the raw string or `prettyJson(value)`. This is the raw JSON seen in Chat. - The live variant is the `metadataOf(item).live === true` branch (`.live-activity-card`). - Card styling lives in `desktop/src/styles.css` (`.activity-card` ~L1093, `.activity-raw` ~L1176, `.activity-data` ~L1192). - Raw JSON is already preserved elsewhere: `RunDetailsInspector.tsx`, `RawJsonView.tsx`, `runDetails.ts` (Raw tab). - Streaming data already reaches the client: `ModelToolEventV1::Progress` → `content_delta("progress", …)` (`desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/run_events.rs` ~L1212) → `activityProjection.ts` merges `channel === "progress"` into `span.progress` (~L199) and `spanItem` folds it into `body`, with `live: isBusy(span.status)`. No new backend contract is required for streaming text. - Non-text results already have a renderer: `ImageAttachments.tsx` plus `toolImageAttachments` in `activityProjection.ts` (~L299) for `tool.image.read` / `tool.screenshot`. ## In scope 1. **Header.** Keep the tool icon and the status chip. Keep the existing capability id, and add the real tool behind it in brackets — `tool.shell.host (bash)`, `tool.shell.host (powershell)`. Resolve the bracketed name from a static `capabilityId → display name` map in the presenter, with the shell dialect taken from the host platform; an unmapped id falls back to the capability id alone. 2. **Input.** Show one formatted line summarising the actual arguments passed to the tool — not raw JSON. Format per argument shape (command, path, pattern, query) rather than dumping the payload. When the content is multiline, add an expand control that grows the field to the current maximum input height with scrollbars, still formatted rather than raw. 3. **Output.** Show the actual output the tool produced. Streaming text (shell job output, grep results) renders incrementally as the tool produces it. Default height 4 rows; an expand button grows it to 10 rows with a scrollbar; the view always auto-scrolls to the end. 4. **Non-text output.** When the output is not text, render the result where possible (reuse `ImageAttachments`) or show a compact status of the result instead of JSON. 5. Keep the existing selection/"Details" path, path actions on file tool cards, and "Inspect source record". ## Out of scope - No change to backend tool execution, the semantic event contract, or result payload schemas. - Run details is unchanged and remains the place for the exact redacted JSON. - No change to tool ordering, status derivation, attribution, or the projection contract itself. Card expansion state and the renderer registry remain owned by Conversation & Card Presenter — extend them, do not duplicate. ## Acceptance criteria - AC1: A tool card header shows the capability id followed by the real tool in brackets (for example `tool.shell.host (bash)`), and an unmapped capability id degrades to the id with no empty brackets. - AC2: A single-argument tool call renders its input as one formatted line, with no raw `{"…"}` JSON on the collapsed card. - AC3: Multiline input offers an expand control; expanded, the field is capped at the current maximum input height and scrolls. - AC4: Output shows the tool's own text, and a running tool's text grows as progress deltas arrive without a manual refresh or a re-open of the card. - AC5: Output defaults to 4 rows, expands to 10 rows with a scrollbar, and keeps auto-scrolling to the newest line while streaming. - AC6: An image-producing tool renders the image; a non-text, non-image result renders a compact status rather than a JSON blob. - AC7: The tool icon and status chip still render, and the Run details Raw tab still shows the exact redacted JSON. - AC8: Tests cover AC1–AC7 (extending `activityProjection.test.ts` and the ConversationTimeline rendering tests); existing `RawJsonView` / `MarkdownContent` behaviour is unchanged.

data.title: Rework the Chat tool-call card: human-readable header, formatted arguments, and live output
